brief: Syz's weekly chart pack frames the week around one causal chain: September's composite PMI rose to 58.4 (strongest since July 2021) and jobless claims and new home sales beat, which combined with hawkish Fed speakers and diesel-export-ban chatter to reinforce inflation and rate-hike expectations, which drove a Treasury selloff (a weak five-year auction at 5.033%, the highest since 2006; the 10-year above 5.20%, highest since July 2007; the 30-year above 5.5%) and widened investment-grade and high-yield credit spreads. October hike odds rose to 70%. The dollar rallied to its highest since July as real yields hit their highest since 2008, pressuring gold, though bitcoin rallied above $87k. AI-driven gains (Meta's Muse app, computing demand) concentrated equity strength in tech while the Russell 2000 declined and small caps lagged. Beyond this frame, the note reports without arguing on Nvidia and SpaceX credit spreads widening, Oracle's Project Jupiter construction delays, SoftBank's junk-bond raise for OpenAI, Middle East oil-shock absorption, Apollo's investor-withdrawal limits, and Trump's warming relationship with Nvidia's Huang.
